exposure: history of low pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A) in an initial pregnancy
low PAPP-A in the first pregnancy followed by normal PAPP-A in the second pregnancy
cohort: The study included 124 patients who underwent first trimester screening for PAPP-A in two consecutive pregnancies.
finding: Patients with recurrent low PAPP-A did not show a significantly higher rate of IUGR or preeclampsia compared to patients with normal PAPP-A in the second pregnancy, suggesting a similar risk of adverse neonatal outcomes.
